entries.name: Bent Over Barbell Row
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: the torso was held about 40 degrees above level. Source-bound side-view draft: hinged over soft knees with a straight back until the trunk is almost level, the bar hanging under the shoulders on straight arms; the trunk and legs do not move while the bar is pulled up and back to the body with the elbows leading, a squeeze, and a slower lowering to a full hang. The bar is seen end-on. Not drawn: the overhand grip.
entries.summary: Hinged forward with a straight back until the torso is almost level, pull the bar from a full hang up to the body with the torso still, squeeze, then lower slowly.

frames.caption: Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, bend the knees slightly and hinge forward with the back straight until the torso is almost level with the floor and the bar hangs under the shoulders.
Keeping the torso still and the elbows close to the body, pull the bar up to the body.
Squeeze the back. Lead with the elbows.
Lower the bar slowly to a full hang.
Back straight, torso still.

entries.name: Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: no bar or plates were drawn. Source-bound side-view draft: one end of the bar is braced on the floor behind the athlete and the loaded end is in front; hinged over slightly bent knees, the near hand grips the shaft just behind the plates and the free hand rests on the thigh above the knee. The trunk does not move while the bar swings up about its braced end until the plates reach the lower chest, a squeeze, and a slower lowering that stops short of the floor. One arm is shown; the last caption carries the change of arms.
entries.summary: Hinged beside a bar braced at its far end, one hand just behind the plates and the other on the knee, pull the bar up until the plates reach the lower chest, squeeze, lower slowly, then change arms.

frames.caption: Load one end of a barbell and brace the other end in a corner, then hinge forward with the knees slightly bent, grip the bar just behind the plates with one hand and rest the other hand on the knee.
Keeping the torso still and the elbow in, pull the bar straight up until the plates reach the lower chest.
Squeeze. Elbow close to the body.
Lower slowly without letting the plates rest on the floor.
Complete the repetitions, then change arms.

entries.name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: the bent-over family body with a dumbbell in each hand rowing together on the shared ladder. Standard two-dumbbell setup chosen from the template; listed in the daily review. The flat back is the fix that was needed: the spine ran 32.0 degrees above horizontal, which reads as a good morning rather than a row, and now runs 6.0. The head sits 9.00 along the spine from the neck and 0.00 off the spine line, so "head in line with the trunk" was already true and is preserved rather than re-claimed. The dumbbells hang straight down from the new shoulder and the pull brings them to the ribs. The elbow is re-solved on the shoulder circle per frame, so the upper arm (12.5) and forearm (12.0) hold their length by construction. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a bent-over two-dumbbell row, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Flat back, dumbbells hanging straight under the shoulders.
Pull the elbows back past the ribs.
Dumbbells at the ribs, back still flat.
Hold at the ribs with the trunk level.
Lower the dumbbells back under control.
Back to a full hang with the spine level.

entries.name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row With Palms In
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: the two-dumbbell bent-over row with the bells drawn standing VERTICAL so the palms-in grip is visible; the palms stay in through the pull. Standard palms-in setup chosen from the template; listed in the daily review. The flat back is the fix that was needed: the spine ran 32.0 degrees above horizontal and now runs 6.0. The palms-in grip keeps the same flat trunk and takes a shorter, tighter pull that stops nearer the body, which is what separates it from the base on the sheet. The head sits 9.00 along the spine from the neck and 0.00 off the spine line, so "head in line with the trunk" was already true and is preserved rather than re-claimed. The dumbbells hang straight down from the new shoulder and the pull brings them to the ribs. The elbow is re-solved on the shoulder circle per frame, so the upper arm (12.5) and forearm (12.0) hold their length by construction. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a bent-over two-dumbbell row with palms in, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Flat back, palms turned in, dumbbells hanging.
Draw the elbows back close to the ribs.
Dumbbells tight to the body, spine still level.
Hold the squeeze with the trunk flat.
Lower the dumbbells back under control.
Back to a full hang with the spine level.
